newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Yellow River sees longest dry stretch.
newsitem.headline: China's Yellow River sees longest dry stretch.

text.p: Drought and increased water use along China's Yellow River have created a record dry stretch on the waterway and threaten crops and fish species, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
The river's lower reaches in eastern Shandong province had been dry since June 23 after drought hit middle and upper reaches amid increased water use by local residents, Xinhua said.
"Hydrologists in the province said the dry-up... has extended beyond its border to neighbouring Henan province, creating the lengthiest dry bed the river has ever seen," the agency said.
Drought had plagued many areas along the river in Shandong, causing an estimated 1.4 billion yuan ($168.7 million) in annual industrial and agricultural losses, it said.
The Yellow River, the nation's second longest, originates on the lofty Qinghai-Tibet plateau and is known as "China's sorrow" for its devastating floods during the rainy season.
This year's drought was particularly severe and authorities were stepping up their efforts to deal with it, Xinhua said.
"The seriousness of this year's dry-river spell has grabbed the attention of government officials and experts who are working full force to alleviate the situation," it said.
The drying up of the river bed was threatening some species of fish with extinction and making nearby areas more susceptible to sandstorms or wind damage, it said.

Hydrologists had also warned that the dry spell could shrink the river bed and reduce the waterway's discharge capacity during the flooding season, thus posing greater risks to flood-prone areas, it said.
